text:
maria: Heads up — canary for release v1.12.0 failed the SBOM provenance/signature check. deploy-bot flagged an unverified signature on org/crypto-lib@2.3.1. Do we pin, rollback, or request an exception?

deploy-bot: [AUTO] sbom-scan: canary build: v1.12.0-canary-42
packages with flags:
- org/crypto-lib@2.3.1 : signature=MISMATCH : provenance=unverified
- com/utils@1.4.0 : ok

kevin: Noted. First step: quarantine the canary traffic and stop the rollout. We need the build artifact digest and the SBOM file. Can someone attach the SBOM export from CI? :mag:

maria: attaching minimal info inline — CI artifact digest: sha256:abc123...
SBOM snippet:
```
name: org/crypto-lib
version: 2.3.1
signature: absent
source: https://ci.redwood/example/binaries/crypto-lib-2.3.1
```

kevin: Looks like the signature isn't present, not a mismatch. That means the publisher step didn't sign the artifact or signature got stripped. We should treat as unverified provenance. Policy says: block rollout unless a documented mitigation exists.

sophia: We can roll the canary back to v1.11.9 digest (sha256:deadbeef) immediately and keep the change window open for the triage. Can QA run regression on the rollback?

linda: Yes, QA can run the quick regression suite on the rollback in the next 30m. Ping me when the canary is pinned/rolled back.

omar: From a compliance perspective, exceptions require a signed mitigation plan and approval from Security + Legal if data plane exposure risk. I don't recommend approving a blanket exception for unsigned provenance.

maria: Proposed plan:
1) Roll canary back to v1.11.9 (sha256:deadbeef) now to reduce blast radius.
2) Create ticket (REL-5234) for supply-chain triage: verify publisher signing and rebuild+resign.
3) Pin service route to older digest for canary for 2 hours, then reassess.
4) Hold global rollout until security signoff or successful re-signed artifact deployed.

kevin: +1 to that plan. Also add: collect CI logs for the publish step and check for signer key rotation or CI job failure. If signer key rotated, we need to coordinate with infra to rekey or trust the new key.

sophia: I'll run the rollback command and pin, then post status. Command I'll run: `rbctl pin service/web-frontend sha256:deadbeef --env=canary --reason="SBOM unverified"`

maria: @linda please confirm regression once done. @kevin & @omar I'll assign REL-5234 to Security and Legal respectively.

linda: regression started — smoke passing so far (10/10 checks). Will update in 15m. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [ACTION] rollback initiated by sophia: service/web-frontend -> sha256:deadbeef ; canary traffic switched at 1749998810

kevin: I'll start the triage. If we can get a re-signed artifact within the hour and QA signs off, we can opt to redeploy a signed build to canary and resume gradual rollout. If not, keep the pin and escalate.

omar: I created a temporary compliance note in REL-5234 (link: https://tickets.redwood/REL-5234) documenting decision and mitigation steps. No legal objections to rollback.

maria: Final decision for now: rollback canary (done), pin canary to previous digest, open ticket REL-5234 for triage and signing, hold global rollout until Security signs off. I'll draft a short release note blurb to explain the pause.

sophia: Done — canary pinned and traffic switched. Will keep monitoring metrics.

linda: Regression complete, nothing unexpected. Marking QA review as passed for the rollback.

kevin: I'll update REL-5234 with triage findings. If signing failure is isolated to the publish job, we'll re-run the signing pipeline and push a signed artifact; if it's a key issue, we'll follow key-rotation playbook.

maria: Thanks everyone. Action items: sophia (rollback/pin) — done, linda (qa) — passed, kevin (sec) — triage + sign, omar (legal) — oversight on ticket. We'll reconvene in #eng-releases once REL-5234 has status. :thumbsup:
